description: Expose every cartographer capability through proto+Connect-RPC with CLI and UI as translation layers; no REST/JSON workarounds permitted.

requirements.description: All cartographer capabilities must be exposed through proto+Connect-RPC service definitions (AC-PROTO-FIRST). CLI commands must map 1:1 to proto methods with no intermediate REST/JSON translation layer (AC-CLI-PROTO-PARITY). The UI must consume only generated Connect clients (AC-UI-PROTO-PARITY). Proto files must be registered in a registry-driven registration system (AC-PROTO-REGISTRY). REST/JSON workarounds are forbidden. All cross-scenario calls to go-code-graph and typescript-code-graph also use Connect-RPC.
requirements.title: Connect-RPC Proto-First Service Definitions with CLI and UI Parity

validation.notes: AC-PROTO-FIRST: Every cartographer capability (extract, detect, resolve, apply, history, stats) has a corresponding proto RPC definition
AC-CLI-PROTO-PARITY: Each CLI command invokes exactly one proto method and passes its flags as proto request fields
AC-CLI-PROTO-PARITY: No CLI command constructs a raw HTTP request or JSON payload directly
AC-UI-PROTO-PARITY: UI source contains no fetch/axios calls to cartographer endpoints; only generated Connect client calls
AC-PROTO-REGISTRY: A new proto file added to the registry is automatically included in generated client/server code without manual registration steps
Cross-scenario Connect-RPC call from cartographer to go-code-graph fixture server returns a valid graph response
Cross-scenario Connect-RPC call from cartographer to typescript-code-graph fixture server returns a valid graph response
CLI round-trip: arch-cart detect invokes the DetectConflicts RPC and returns proto-shaped conflict envelopes
A new capability added to cartographer is immediately available in both CLI and UI without a separate API integration task
No REST/JSON workaround is merged; code review enforces this via lint rule or CI check

title: Connect-RPC + CLI + UI Parity
